To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of ESS in the electricity system is beneficial for the system operator, since it provides additional revenue, and it reduces the need for conventional generation to provide ancillary services.
the main benefits of ESS are the provision of ancil- lary services, and the ability to reduce the wear-and-tears of conventional generation sources, which are the most expensive units to ramp.
the main benefits for a system operator are the reduction of the cost of ramping conventional units and the reduction of the provision of anciliary services by conventional units.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model to evaluate the cost-benefit of ESS in a system operator perspective, taking into account environmental concerns.

the evaluation of the effects of integrating storage systems in the electricity system from the perspective of an operator, taking into consideration the cost of carbon dioxide emissions, and the interactions of ESS with conventional generation sources.
the economic analysis of power system operations, taking into account environmental concerns, and the integration of ESS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of ESS units in a power system with a high level of RES penetration, allows to reduce the cost of the system operation, by reducing the cost of conventional generation units.
the integration of ESS into the network, with the aim of increasing the penetration of RES, is economically viable.
the integration of ESS in the network reduces the costs derived from the variability of RES, and the wear and tear of conventional generation units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of ESS can be a good option for system operators, as long as the cost of the ESS is lower than the cost of the ancillary services provided by conventional sources.
the use of ESS is a good option to increase the penetration of RES in the system.
the integration of ESS units in the system can be a cost-efficient solution for a power system operator, as they can reduce the cost of the system while increasing the reliability of the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of C02 emissions can be used as an important tool for the evaluation of the economic benefits of ESS.
ESS can be an important asset in the electricity system to provide flexibility, and thus, reduce the costs associated with the integration of high levels of renewable energy.
the inclusion of environmental costs in the objective function of the SC-OPF is an effective way to account for the effects of CO2 emissions on the system.
